items.followUp: A metal object has a mass of 2 kg and a volume of 0.001 m³. Find its density.

rubric.why: Shows the density relation and converts both given quantities to SI units.
rubric.description: Writes density = mass ÷ volume and converts the mass and volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula and both SI conversions.

rubric.why: Gives the correct calculated density with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 500 g = 0.5 kg; volume, V = 200 cm³ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³.

items.followUp: State Newton’s third law of motion and give two examples from everyday life.

rubric.description: States Newton’s third law: forces occur as equal and opposite action–reaction pairs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the law’s complete relationship.

rubric.why: Recognises the action and reaction involved in walking.
rubric.description: Explains that a person pushes the ground backward and the ground pushes the person forward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct walking example.

rubric.why: Recognises the action and reaction involved in gun recoil.
rubric.description: Explains that the bullet moves forward while the gun recoils backward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct gun-recoil example.

rubric.why: Recognises the action and reaction involved in swimming.
rubric.description: Explains that the swimmer pushes water backward and the water pushes the swimmer forward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct third example.

modelAnswer: Newton’s third law states that when one body exerts a force on another body, the second body exerts an equal and opposite force on the first body.
Walking: a person pushes the ground backward, and the ground pushes the person forward.
Gun recoil: the bullet moves forward, and the gun recoils backward.
Swimming: a swimmer pushes water backward, and the water pushes the swimmer forward.
